note: Descriptions of the source landing-page templates: the most detailed written record of layout + motion craft in the pack. Inspiration; no code.

templates.title: Aerra
templates.description: A six-section landing page for a single finished house standing alone on a mountain slope. It opens behind a white curtain whose percentage counter runs 0 → 100 along the bottom edge and then leaves through a rounded hole that grows out of the sheet until it clears the viewport; only then does the hero play, the brand name writing itself in letter by letter at 801px behind a cut-out dusk photograph, then the headline word by word, then the subtitle, the button and the caption. Scrolling splits the wordmark — alternating letters climb 14rem and 5rem against the scroll while a white-to-transparent gradient runs down each glyph — and every photograph on the page drifts against the scroll inside its own clip box. The about block pairs a quote card laid over the facade with a drag-to-rotate turntable: a video that is never played but seeked frame by frame, playing itself through once on arrival and draggable by the surface or by a pill scrubber, either of which cancels the playthrough rather than fighting it. Three statistics count up out of a blur that resolves off the same spring that drives the number. The location section is a night photograph of the ridge with a site plan painted into it by the cursor — a raw-WebGL pass keeping an 84 × 56 heat grid on the CPU and sampling it NEAREST, so the grid's own cells are the pixels of the reveal. The audience block is a 3 × 3 grid of frosted glass cards with the centre and both counter-diagonal cells left empty, and a matte-black three.js mark travelling the whole height of the section behind them, turning twice, clipped by the section's own edges so it rises from under one block and slides away under the next. It closes on a frosted contact panel with three underlined fields whose labels are their own placeholders.
vibes: a house alone on a slope, sold slowly and with a straight face
eight hundred pixels of a name standing behind a building
a counter that walks along the bottom of the screen and then drops off it
a window opening in a white sheet instead of the sheet fading
letters that come apart as you scroll and never stop being a word
turning a facade in your hand at the speed of your own drag
painting a site plan into a photograph with the cursor
a black mark drifting the length of the page behind glass
numbers that resolve out of a blur exactly as they stop counting
a headline whose first half is dimmed so the second half lands

templates.title: AI Creator
templates.description: A one-page site for an AI creator who makes vertical video ads, set on porcelain (#f0f0f0) and electric blue (#0051ff) in three faces — a light display serif for the names, a text serif for the two lines that speak, a sans for the small print. Its subject is a photogrammetry bust of the creator rendered live in WebGL on a white studio stage, and there is ONE canvas, one context, pinned for a runway of seven viewports on which the whole page is told: the name is set across the full width of the screen BEHIND the canvas and the bust stands in front of it, covering the middle of the word; it ARRIVES when the loading curtain lifts — approaching from nearer the camera and burning in patch by patch, every fragment discarded until a drifting noise field falls under the level, with an electric-blue ember and a pale lick along each front — then sways, tilts towards the cursor, and wherever the pointer passes a hard-edged white mark washes the texture off and reveals the welded topology underneath, on the model and on the ground alike. Scroll, and a hard line bows up the screen (it bends with how fast you are travelling, flat at rest) and the white stage becomes a live fire-front field in five blues — char behind the line, ember on it, licks above, the fuel scrolling past a fixed threshold so the front advances for ever, leaning toward the hand and smearing into a wake behind it; below the line the bust dissolves into the field and only its mesh carries it, hairlines with lit junction sparks, a lamp held to it under the cursor, while "One face, Four hundred takes" is painted into the frame by the scene itself, behind the subject, resolving letter by letter in a scrambled order. A second line opens the model for good and the mesh's junctions TRAVEL across the stage — ranked by column and matched like to like — to assemble an authored 3D mark that reads "AI", whose star spins in place; chrome pours up through the letters from the bottom with a bright waterline, blooms, reflects a painted studio of bands and strips, and the word turns a full revolution while "What lands in your Drive" hangs four deliverables under a rule the scene draws beneath the word. Then seven photographs travel down the screen round a BOX seen edge-on, each card cut into eighteen bands so it folds over the crease rather than tipping, with the three process steps inking in across them in reading order; and the closing screen rides up on a 36-degree tilted blue plane that lands flat — "Book a batch" behind a cutout of the same bust, its foot already dissolved into the accent, the invitation and a magnetic e-mail pill leading and lagging against the panel. A floating pill of four section links opens out of a disc from the centre of the screen once the first screen is behind you and leaves before the plane climbs. A phone gets a lite path: the decimated bust turning a fifth of a revolution on a short runway, and the two later screens as stills of the scene itself, drifting against the scroll on a spring.
vibes: a name you can only read around the person standing in front of it
a face burning in patch by patch out of the blue
a white mark that strips the skin off and shows the mesh underneath
a fire front in five blues creeping up the screen as you scroll
hairlines with lit junctions carrying a head where the texture used to be
a wireframe that leaves the body and assembles into the word AI
chrome pouring up through letters with a bright waterline
photographs folding over a crease as they travel past
a blue plane tilting up to land with the invitation already on it
an e-mail address that leans toward your hand
a pill of links opening out of a disc from the middle of the screen

templates.title: AI Studio
templates.description: A cinematic scroll-driven AI showreel that lives on a fixed black stage: a full-bleed mesh-gradient hero card flips into a cosine-sorted 4-card product carousel, opens into a 34k-point violet particle sphere, hands off to a horizontal portfolio video rail wrapped in an aurora glow, then flies the camera through a parallax image grid into a chrome brand-star finale — every phase scrubbed by one scroll clock.

templates.title: Altitude
templates.description: A single-screen hospitality hero shot at night: a looping starry-sky video is drawn by a WebGL2 fluid solver that also warps it — an invisible stirring point orbits a spring-lagged cursor and marbles lantern-yellow and sky-blue ink into a vortex that drags and chromatically splits the picture where it moves, then dies away within a second of the cursor stopping. Over it a Gilda Display line rises letter by letter out of a blur under a left-to-right fade mask, a glass enquiry capsule and a glass stats bar lift on springs, and two hairline column rules rule themselves down the frame — all released at once by a comet-field preloader that counts to 100 and opens the page like an aperture.
vibes: a lantern in the dark
night sky you forgot existed
ink marbling under the cursor
quiet, expensive hospitality
one screen, nothing else

templates.title: Artefakt
templates.description: A one-page concept for a technical outerwear label, drawn entirely on a 10px lattice of near-black cells and pure-black hairlines that runs the whole height of the document and brightens in squares under the cursor — one grid, painted once, with every panel on the page wearing an opaque copy of it so they light up in phase. Its subject is a lacquered, iridescent black puffer rendered live in WebGL, and there is ONE canvas and one context for it: the garment is framed in the hero and then TRAVELS as you scroll — growing from 570 to 795 units, dropping, sliding left and turning forty degrees — into the second screen, where it comes to rest full-bleed behind five numbered specification rows. It answers the cursor the whole way, turntable on one axis and roll on the other, and its sleeves and belt straps trail the turn on their own springs; a second, pinned instance runs off the bottom-left corner of the FAQ screen, approaching its rest pose on scroll position alone so it runs backwards when the reader does. Between them: four product cards that tilt towards the cursor with the garment standing off the face in its own 3D layer and the tag chips trading for a SHOP NOW link; a pinned technology stage whose scroll SCRUBS a sixty-one-frame reel of the jacket's five materials exploding apart, with a single specification card walking down them on a leader line drawn to the layer it names. A chromed ARTEFAKT wordmark sits behind the hero at a fifth opacity with a torch travelling over it — the cursor's own disc where there is a cursor, a slanted sweep on a 7.4s cycle where there is not. Every label on the page decodes out of random glyphs, on arrival, on hover and on focus, and the whole thing opens behind a curtain gated on real readiness — fonts resolved, window loaded, model compiled — whose four corner brackets scale away as it lifts.
vibes: a grid that lights up in squares wherever you point
a black jacket that is somehow blue when the light catches it
the product walking from one screen to the next as you scroll
sleeves that catch up a beat after the garment turns
five materials pulling apart under your thumb on the scroll wheel
a hairline drawn from a card to the exact layer it is describing
labels resolving out of static as they arrive
corner brackets closing on whatever you point at
a chromed wordmark you can only read where the light is
cards that lean towards your hand with the garment floating off the face
nothing filled — every surface is the grid, every edge a hairline

templates.title: Artist
templates.description: A long-scroll monochrome portfolio for a fine artist — Playfair Display serif over near-black ink on white, dashed hairlines, pinned CTAs, and a stately cadence of statement, works, principles, process and exhibitions.

templates.title: Ascend
templates.description: A single-page immersive SaaS landing experience: one fixed, photoreal WebGL earth — day/night city-lights shader, drifting cloud shells, atmosphere halo, starfield and radar-ping markers, composited through bloom and a corner-flame pass — sits behind four glass sections (hero, features, live-dashboard showcase, CTA/footer) while a single scroll clock zooms and swings the planet across the page.

templates.title: Auralis
templates.description: A one-page scroll film for an AI-native design studio: the entire site is one pinned WebGL void — a silver-grey haze where each act is a wireframe containment lattice floating in the fog (no ground, no podium, no fixtures) — and scroll drives a single continuous camera shot through four acts. On the preloader hand-off, ~32 000 tiny white spheres fly in from around the camera and assemble into a volumetric X trailing pink comet streaks, its lattice weaving itself closed segment by segment around the nearly-finished figure; the X floats, tilts toward the cursor, repels around it, then bursts into violet ribbon streamers strung along the flight corridor while the camera dollies forward with a gentle ~15° mid-flight bank. A second lattice carries a ~50 000-bead hand that scans in bottom-up while pirouetting a full eased 360°; its own particles then crumble through meandering bright pink streams onto a huge rippling grid curtain tilted into the fog, and a tilted film wipe sweeps a separately-framed finale in over it — a ~150 000-particle tree growing bottom-up inside its own weaving cage, pink fireflies climbing around the crown, the tree camera drifting on a slow orbit, under an ENVISION heading and a glass contact bar. Every resting figure breathes (a GPU violet flow band + whole-form sway), every built lattice turns forever and sparkles with pink impulses. Over the canvas: three blended light-flare layers that stage their own entrance, parallax the cursor and bank with the camera, film grain, a glass header, and per-act overlays whose type reveals letter-by-letter through a blur-and-lift spring engine, paced to land with the fly-in.
vibes: one unbroken camera shot through a silver studio
an X of beads that bursts into violet ribbons as you dive through it
a hand assembling out of fog on a metal podium
thousands of particles crumbling into a rippling curtain
a film wipe that slides the finale in over a frozen wave
glass UI floating over a room made of light and dust
the scene is the site — the copy just visits

templates.title: Baseline
templates.description: A bright, confident tennis-academy landing page in royal blue on white — hero over a court, a trust bar, program cards, facilities, stat counters and testimonials, closing on a footer and contact modal.

templates.title: Brewns
templates.description: A one-page site for brewns, a specialty coffee house in San Francisco, set on near-black (#070707) and bone (#f1f1ef) surfaces that alternate down the page, with one fixed header recolouring itself to whichever it is passing over, in four faces — Geist bold and semibold, uppercase, for every headline and lede; Space Mono for every label, eyebrow, nav link, price, address and the printed receipt; Allura for one script word, "moment", laid over the hero headline; and one amber accent spent only on a pulsing dot. The page opens behind a preloader that is a DRAWN paper cup filling with coffee — the level rises on real load signals (mount, fonts, load), the count under it reads the level, and when the cup is full the coffee pours and the whole panel is cut from the top down at the pour's own rate, so the screen leaves as one body of liquid. The hero is a thin-film-interference WebGL2 gradient in coffee browns (Opalesce: one fullscreen triangle, a domain-warped fbm ground, a cosine film that MULTIPLIES the ramp, and a three-node pointer rig whose wake reconstructs a tapered trail with no frame of history) behind a Draco model of a bag of beans and a takeaway cup on plain three.js — fitted to exactly the rectangle a product photograph once occupied, lit by four baked softboxes on a black ground plus three keys held sixty degrees off the lens so the printed black stays black, rendered through Khronos' neutral tone curve at a 1.5 pixel-ratio floor. It rises into place as the panel drains, turning out of a quarter-radian into its pose; it leans toward the cursor, the cup further and sooner than the bag; the piece under the pointer lifts on a damped spring with a small twist and its own glass card appears on the header's line; grab it and it turns under your hand a degree per two pixels and keeps spinning when you let go; and it sinks by a fifth of its height as the hero scrolls away. The headline slides out of its clip line by line, the script word writes itself under one sweeping clip, and the info bar assembles left to right with its hairlines drawing between the groups and its hours rolling into place digit by digit. The menu is the light half: the brand swirl grows behind it out of four soft blobs that open in sequence and finish together, VIEW FULL MENU slides a tilted receipt in behind itself on hover, and four bordered product cards rise on a stagger while their photographs lag behind on a scroll scrub and the whole card leans toward the pointer on a perspective. The locations block is a clock face with an iced latte at its centre carrying three motions on three nested elements — a lean toward the cursor, a parallax that resolves as the block arrives, and a turn to thirty-eight degrees as it leaves — with the swirl filling right to left this time so the two blocks read as one stroke. The philosophy block runs the same gradient under a five-stop scrim with the cup alone standing where the board draws it, tilted, cut by the section's bottom edge, spinning about its own tilted axis with the scroll, and thirty-four coffee beans (sixteen on a phone) floating weightless behind it on a hand-written rigid-body field: a slow air wander, a cursor that pushes the air out of its way and leaves a wake, elastic bean-on-bean and bean-on-cup hits with friction that turn a glancing hit into spin, walls at the frustum, and a vortex that wheels the beans about the view axis at the speed you scroll. The order block is a 1440×800 stage scaled to cover the viewport: a photograph drifting in on a parallax, a thermal printer, and a receipt — HTML and CSS, never an image — feeding out of its slot in forty-six jerks as the block rises, its barcode settling from a ragged skyline to its printed height once it has cleared the housing. A 385px footer band closes with every line rising out of its own mask, the swirl fading in behind, and hairlines drawing left to right and top to bottom.
vibes: a paper cup filling with coffee while the page loads, then pouring the whole screen away
a bag of beans and a cup you can pick up, turn under your hand and let spin
the piece under your pointer lifting a little, with its own price card appearing on the header's line
a coffee-brown film of colour travelling out behind your cursor
the brand swirl growing out of four soft blobs as the menu arrives
product cards leaning toward your hand with their photographs lagging a beat behind
a receipt sliding in behind VIEW FULL MENU when you point at it
an iced latte turning on a clock face as you scroll past it
coffee beans drifting weightless behind a tilted cup, bouncing off it and each other
a thermal printer feeding your receipt out in jerks as the block rises
a barcode settling from a jagged skyline to its printed height
prices and opening hours rolling into place digit by digit

templates.title: Clair
templates.description: A dark, brutal-technical AI product hero: white Mulish type over a pure-black stage, an indigo-violet swirl running full-bleed behind it, and a live WebGL glass lightning bolt — dispersive, amber-lit, leaning toward the cursor — with a per-letter headline cascade and per-word copy reveals released by an intro preloader.

templates.title: Clarix
templates.description: A 28-viewport cinematic single-scroll page for an AI creative studio, driven end-to-end by one scroll clock. A Draco-compressed 3D object — shaded with a holographic fresnel rim, flowing curved light-lines and a per-pixel ASCII dither that morphs squares into circles as the colour runs warm — flies through six choreographed phases: a corner-anchored hero, three giant words that arc past the lens on a perspective curve, a frosted glass panel of statistics, a full-height left-column feature split, a particle wordmark assembled from the logo's own alpha channel plus 3,500 ambient drifters, and a centred outro that lifts a glass footer into frame. Behind all of it, a full-screen procedural ASCII field of rounded boxes pulses blue → cyan → hot-pink → red and ripples away from the cursor. A stepped 000→100 odometer preloader with a shattering iridescent blob gates the entrance, then a screen-space reveal circle carves the model into existence.
vibes: cinematic 28-screen scroll film on a white page
iridescent holographic object dissolving into an ASCII halftone grid
airy editorial whitespace with corner-pinned index labels
frosted glass panels sliding over a live gradient field
wordmark shattering into a drifting particle galaxy

templates.title: Codescan
templates.description: A studio site that is one continuous WebGL shot eight screens tall, watched through a CRT. It opens on a dark room where a figure stands with its back to you facing a wall of fourteen televisions, each playing its own clip; the lens drifts after the cursor on a heavy spring, and hovering a set raises it — and everything stacked on it, in a staggered cascade — turns it about its own footprint, and racks focus onto it, while a chip on the cursor types out the name of the work on its glass, or says 'Coming soon…' without an arrow over the sets showing nothing. Scrolling flies the camera level down the room, dissolving the figure rather than steering round it, out the far side of the wall and along a corridor of fog where two lines stand at different depths and lift out of the haze one after the other, letter by letter, as real geometry rather than a caption. Five televisions then come at the lens out of the fog and assemble into a ring, turned by Previous and Next, the work's name and tags re-springing with the picture. Two full-window black panels slide up over the room — the team on a draggable 3D card cylinder you can throw and let settle, then the studio's own words on a trail of three cards — the first arriving as a wave of ragged pixels climbing the window and the last leaving the same way, uncovering the closing shot: the same figure again, close and from behind, holding still while the lens pulls back past him, one fixed television at his shoulder carrying a Start a Project still, the horizon deliberately off level, and a hairline rule under the words that is cut exactly where the set's silhouette begins and follows it as the hover turns it. Over all of it sits a fixed instrument frame — hairline rules stopping short of two-pixel corner brackets, an fps counter, a tally light, the date and a running clock.
vibes: a room lit by nothing but the screens in it
a figure with its back to you, watching fourteen televisions at once
hover a set and the whole column above it lifts
the lens pulls focus onto whatever you point at
flying past the wall into fog with two sentences standing in it
televisions coming at you out of the haze and forming a row
a wave of black squares climbing the window to take the room away
photographs on a cylinder you can throw and watch settle
the horizon deliberately off level for the last shot
a rule that stops exactly where the television starts, and follows it
an fps counter nobody asked for, and the page is better for it
the whole thing watched through glass that never lets you forget it

templates.title: Cortex
templates.description: A single-screen AI-agency hero: a giant gradient wordmark and lead copy over a live WebGL prism-streak shader, chromatic light filaments that sway to the cursor above pure black, unveiled by a curtain preloader.

templates.title: Creative Director
templates.description: A cinematic pure-black art-director portfolio: a full-screen hero video lit by a mouse-following molten-orange glow with a dot-matrix scramble wordmark, sitting over one continuous raymarched WebGL lava backdrop that blurs and blooms behind glass case-study cards, a services grid, a horizontal project carousel, and a GET IN TOUCH footer — all on a single Lenis scroll clock with spring reveals and film grain.

templates.title: Creative Studio
templates.description: A dark, solar studio hero: one continuous WebGL scene — an additive particle sun breathing over an fBm aurora, finished with UnrealBloom — sits behind a frosted near-black glass panel with a cut-out window, framed by nested orbit rings, while a white-on-black masthead, a per-word headline reveal, and a stat strip ease in after a counting preloader wipes away.

templates.title: Dantora
templates.description: A landing page for a private medical clinic, built around a WebGL DNA helix drawn in green ink on white water. Two point clouds — 40,000 points hugging the double helix and 160,000 more shedding continuously from it — are MULTIPLY-blended, so the dye darkens the pale mint paper rather than glowing on black; the plume is a pure function of a normalised life, born on the strand and pushed outward on an evolving simplex flow, swelling and thinning as it disperses, and both clouds part around a soft ball at the cursor while the camera drifts lazily after it. The helix appears twice, in the hero and behind the contact form. Between them the page is a sequence of transitions as much as blocks: a white band where moving the mouse spawns photographs along the cursor's path, each scaling in where it was dropped and the oldest scaling away; a four-viewport scroll runway whose panel pins while five service cards scrub sideways; an About block that rides up over that pinned panel carrying a parallax banner and four statistics that count out of nothing; a sticky team rail you drag and throw, with a progress bar under it; and a contact block that rides up over the team in turn. It opens behind a brand-green curtain whose ring draws clockwise while the DNA mark fills on a hard 45° diagonal, then clips away bottom-to-top — releasing the hero's copy mid-lift, so the words are already resolving out of their blur as the panel clears them.
vibes: a double helix bleeding ink into white water
dye that swirls outward and thins into nothing, over and over
the strand parting around wherever your cursor is
photographs falling out of the pointer and dissolving behind it
a wall of service cards that moves sideways because you scrolled down
one block climbing up over another instead of following it
numbers arriving out of nowhere and settling without a bounce
a ring drawing itself while a DNA mark fills on the diagonal
copy that comes into focus rather than sliding in
green and lime, and a page that stays white underneath

templates.title: Dringle
templates.description: A light single-screen agency hero: navy type and a violet gradient CTA on a lavender ground, beside a dark rounded media panel where chrome hands and a spinning star render live in WebGL, tilting toward the cursor over a purple-glass video.

templates.title: Evolve
templates.description: A one-screen, jet-black hero for an AI infrastructure company. The subject is a human head and shoulders rendered as a point cloud — tens of thousands of particles lit in the shader by a blue key from front-left and a red rim from back-right (magenta where the lobes overlap), bloomed at deliberately coarse resolution into the haze that fills the frame. The cloud shimmers with a tiny per-point surface drift, turns to follow the pointer on an eased parallax, and particles scatter away from the cursor and spring back behind it, with the far side of the head thinning out through a view-space depth fade. Behind it, an eight-column hairline blueprint grid with plus-shaped crosshairs at rule intersections; over it, an uppercase mono nav in difference blend, a gradient-framed GET STARTED CTA whose five chevrons run a looping cascade on hover, a two-part display headline — 'Engineering / Intelligence' top-left, 'That Evolves / With You.' bottom-right — a mono lead line, and three grid-pinned stats whose figures settle out of scrambled glyphs. Boot is a mono percentage over a hairline gradient track that counts real milestones (fonts + first rendered frame, 6s failsafe), lifts, and only then lets the authored entrance timeline play. Two temporal filters at the end of the composer keep the dense cloud from flickering without touching the artwork.
vibes: a human head made of eighty-seven thousand glowing embers
blue light from one side, red from the other, magenta where they meet
particles that flee your cursor and settle back behind it
a head that turns to watch the pointer cross the room
stat figures decoding themselves out of terminal noise
a blueprint grid the subject stands in front of, not behind
a loading bar that counts real work and refuses to lie
the far side of the skull dissolving into the dark

templates.title: Flowstate
templates.description: A single immersive hero for a deep-work product: a full-bleed WebGL fluid shader paints an oily cyan-to-magenta ink swirl that bursts on load and forever orbits the centre, while an Onest wordmark, glass nav, per-word heading, and a glass waitlist bar float over a near-black abyss.
vibes: ink in water
immersive dark hero
wet neon focus
one bright fluid over a black abyss
calm but alive

templates.title: Forma®
templates.description: A single-viewport studio contact hero laid out gutter-to-gutter on a 30px inset: wordmark + four-item nav on a 770px rail, a two-line 56px headline that wipes in letter by letter from the left, an inline name/email form with a gradient-ring submit disc, and a 350:350:640 card row (metric + spring-filled gradient meter, positioning statement, lavender showcase card with light-trail artwork). The whole middle band is a looping violet-valley video under a WebGL ripple shader — the pointer leaves a wake of expanding sine rings that push the footage along their radius. A percentage preloader with a card-height gradient bar holds the page, then releases one 40→820ms spring cascade across every element.
vibes: quiet expensive studio masthead
one screen, no scroll, everything on the gutter
violet valley footage rippling under the cursor
letter-by-letter headline wipe over a lavender card row
percentage preloader that hands off to a spring cascade
design-system-first agency contact page

templates.title: Fromzero
templates.description: A one-viewport hero for a fictional creative studio ('We make the web look back'). A near-black preloader curtain counts 00→100 under the FROMZER(0) wordmark, then slides straight up to reveal a night mountain valley in WebGL: a video panel showing a human eye floats dead centre, tilting to face the cursor, ringed by six floating planes of live running code — a source file scrolling like an editor, snippets typing themselves out under a blinking caret, build logs streaming with a progress bar — that parallax against the panel by depth. Bright rectangles rain down the video itself. The valley floor is a black lake carrying a real analytic reflection of the panel; the cursor's travel stamps expanding wake rings into it, and the terrain's rock relief breaks the reflection up through its normal maps. The camera drifts on a slow pure dolly, bloom and film grain finish the image. Over the canvas, a poster UI springs in element by element as the curtain leaves: a slate frosted header with an accent CTA, an overline, hairline dividers, a two-line brand-yellow headline that decodes left-to-right through a character scramble, and a white CTA bar with a black arrow box. No scroll — the page is exactly one viewport.
vibes: a screen that watches you back from the middle of a night valley
code raining and compiling in the air around an eye
a black lake that remembers everywhere your cursor has been
the site's reflection rippling across dark water
a headline that decodes itself letter by letter
a preloader curtain that counts to 100 and gets out of the way
one viewport, no scroll — the scene is the site

templates.title: Gravity
templates.description: An independent-studio hero built on one persistent WebGL gravity field: ~96 pastel-glass spheres cluster in the masthead, surrender to real simulated physics and drop, reassemble into a heart, then accelerate past the lens — four full-viewport sections cross-fading over the field on a single scroll clock while the whole palette morphs blue → volt-lime → rose-pink.

templates.title: GringX
templates.description: A jet-black AI-intelligence hero built around a live WebGL nebula orb cradled by floating hands, with a per-letter headline and a bottom band of metrics glowing in electric periwinkle blue.

templates.title: Halcyon
templates.description: A luxury-timepiece brand experience told as one continuous, scroll-driven flight across an endless sea: a single fullscreen fragment shader paints a golden ocean with a brass gate ring, perspective waves, mirrored reflections and drifting cumulus, blending through four biomes — golden hour, smouldering dusk, moonlit night, emerald dawn — while a 3D pocket clock floats dead-centre and materialises out of an oily iridescent dissolve, and four blackletter narrative beats reveal word-by-word over the water, all driven by one scroll clock.

templates.title: Helion
templates.description: A design-studio landing page set inside deep space: one continuous WebGL particle scene that morphs from a galaxy through a plasma burst into an accretion disc and finally assembles the twin-triangle brand mark, with four Mulish-set sections cross-fading over it on a single scroll clock.

templates.title: Kimi
templates.description: A one-page driver site for a Formula 1 rookie — GRIDO1 Racing Systems, Kimi Antonelli, driver_012 — set on a near-white ground (#f7fafb) with pure-black copy, one cyan accent (#02d2e3) and near-black instrument panels, in two faces: a condensed bold display (Oswald) for the 96px name, the mastheads and the stat figures, and a grotesk (Space Grotesk) for everything conversational, all of it uppercase. The first three blocks are a STACK: each pins at the top of the viewport and the next comes out over it while the covered one recedes to 0.9 and darkens by 55%, and the page returns to ordinary flow under the third. The hero is one WebGL canvas behind a masthead, two bracket-cornered panels and a footer row: a depth-parallax photograph of the driver, relit toward the cursor off a normal map, with a Draco Mercedes helmet WORN over it that pitches and yaws two degrees with the pointer through two cascaded filters. The page opens behind a veil — a helmet silhouette filling from the crown and a 4px meter along the foot, both creeping to 70% and completing only when the scene has compiled — then the composition rises 200px into place and the helmet BURNS AWAY crown-to-chin with a glowing cyan front; from there it exists only inside the cursor's recent path, a chain of capsules over the last 72 smoothed pointer positions thresholded hard and warped by scrolling noise so the edge crawls, gated on pointer speed so a resting cursor shows no helmet at all, while the backdrop behind it draws the same mask as two alternating greys banded by the contour field's parity. A faint wireframe wave scans the invisible helmet every 3.1s and animated iso-lines of a four-sine field roll across the whole block. The seam into the dark second block is a CHEQUERED FLAG coming apart — the light ground carries in as solid rows, breaks into a chequerboard and burns off as you scroll, six percent of the squares in the accent. Behind that block's copy sits a 2560×1440 instrument-panel map: an 8,004-dot halftone landmass drawn from a packed lattice, dashed grid axes that crawl one period every seven seconds, a hub with three rings and a slow ping, seven corner marks and the designer's own filled track ribbon; when the block arrives the circuit FILLS FROM THE CHEQUERED FLAG, clockwise, in one six-second lap paced by the path's own curvature — braking through the corners, running away down the straights — as a cyan line with an additive glow and a white filament at its hot head, lighting four turn markers as it passes and cooling to a plain closed lap at rest, after which the cursor becomes a RETICLE over the map, two arms along its own lattice row and column that only open when it settles, the dots squaring up into a chequer wherever the light reaches. A standings plate with a chamfered corner and a turning wire globe types itself in beside it. The timeline is seven photographs in stepped-corner plates on a gapless 1440×2700 stack, a rail down the middle with a white progress thread and a square marker that turns five times over the block, three parallax layers per row that pass through their design position as the row crosses the middle of the screen, years that assemble letter by letter and settle back to 40% after two seconds, plates that inset 5% on hover and dim every other row. The paddock block returns to light: a 96px masthead, the race report, a chamfered dark button whose accent floods along its own path, the portrait bleeding off both ends and melting into a dark band that carries the five-round calendar — cards on the designer's own x, dashed connectors crawling toward the live round, a pulse on its marker and corner brackets that open 5px when it is pointed at — with the hero's contour field marched on a canvas behind everything. The footer is a cyan page edge with a near-black panel inset 16 inside it, the same contours in white at 10%, the helmet-and-suit figure standing off the foot and riding back into place as the page bottoms out, and a nav column resolving letter by letter.
vibes: a helmet that burns off his face while you wait, then lives only where your cursor has just been
a portrait that turns toward the light in your hand

the light ground breaking into a chequered flag and blowing away into the dark

templates.title: Laocoön
templates.description: A single-screen cinematic landing built around one rearing bronze statue: a real-time WebGL scene where a GLB horse is lit chiaroscuro over a liquid-metal wave shader, forge-sparks drifting upward, while the camera orbits 360 degrees on a single scroll clock and the wave palette cools from molten copper into deep sapphire. Four Italiana-set editorial slides fade in and out over the same scroll.

templates.title: Loopstack
templates.description: A single non-scrolling black screen for a closed-beta invite: a Playfair serif headline rises word by word out of its own mask, blurred, over a full-bleed flower film that owns the lower 90% of the viewport, with a soft black scrim bled down from the top edge to hold the type and a rounded black 'Book a demo' pill carrying one pulsing neon-lime live dot. A hairline footer bar floats dead-centre over the video — 'Stay in Touch' / 'Think. Build. Repeat.', socials, four links, copyright — and a 21.9vw 'Loopstack' wordmark sweeps in letter by letter from the left along the bottom edge. A white outline ring is pinned exactly to the cursor while a frosted-glass 'SAY HELLO!' pill trails behind it; both collapse to nothing the moment the pointer reaches the CTA.

templates.title: Lumea
templates.description: A single full-bleed, real-time 3D hero for a design studio: a stone monk meditating on a floating rock pedestal in a near-black void, two glowing amber orbit lines ringing him, inside a slowly turning vertical spiral of ~300 tumbling rock shards. One soft volumetric shaft rakes down onto the figure from high above — no visible source — while white dust motes drift through the dark and the camera circles endlessly on a low, dutch-tilted orbit. The cursor swings the orbit and pushes nearby shards aside; they drift away with real weight (an underdamped spring, heavier for bigger rocks) and settle back. The debris — and only the debris — carries a subtle film-style chromatic fringe, masked per-frame so the monk and rings never split. Over the canvas: a frosted-glass nav pill, a serif headline that blooms in letter-by-letter through blur, a right-hand intro and 'Pitch your idea' line, a bottom sparkle + uppercase tagline, and a big white cursor-trailing ring in difference blend. Boot is a light-mist preloader: a square outline draws itself clockwise while a serif counter climbs — holding at 99% until every shader is genuinely compiled and rendered — then the same square inks black, swallows the screen and fades to reveal the scene.
vibes: a stone monk levitating in a museum-dark void
two rings of amber light orbiting a meditating figure

templates.description: A single non-scrolling studio hero built around a 50 000-point human head rendered in raw WebGL: front-lit from the upper left so the face carves out of the dark, with the shadow side continuously shedding particles that brighten as they stream upward and regenerate at the surface. templates.title: Stride Nine
templates.description: A one-screen hero for a performance running brand. The subject is footage — two sprinters in orange kit at full stride against a deep blue sky, looping silently full-bleed — with the interface drawn on top of it in white line and white capitals: a cropped STRIDE wordmark and hairline-separated tagline top-left, a five-item nav top-right, a 90px three-line headline on authored break points ('Every mile / starts before / the first step.') bottom-left over a mono-weight lead, two square CTAs, a hairline-bracketed assurance row, and a frosted LIVE telemetry card pinned bottom-right. On a fine pointer the footage carries a cursor-driven drag trail: a three-pass WebGL2 chain that displaces the frame through a baked anisotropic turbulence field, smears it with a σ=52px one-dimensional Gaussian in a space rotated so the −18° brand axis IS the buffer's X, then grades and lays the result back over the untouched picture through up to sixteen summed ellipse falloffs and a warm-biased subject gate, so the smear grips the athletes and leaves the sky alone. A second Canvas 2D layer draws up to 72 curved airflow streamlines on the same diagonal in screen blend, and a 28px difference-blend disc floats after the pointer. Load is a dark cover whose wordmark is uncovered by looping speed streaks travelling on that same axis over a bar counting two real milestones (fonts + poster decode, 6s failsafe); it lifts along the diagonal, and only then does the authored entrance run — six uneven streaks crossing the copy block while the nav, eyebrow, headline lines, lead, buttons, assurance row and card arrive in their wake on absolute delays from 120ms to 1240ms.
vibes: two sprinters frozen mid-stride, and the air still moving around them
drag your cursor and the picture smears the way the runners are running
white capitals standing directly on a photograph
a loading screen that is a start line, and lifting it is the step
speed streaks uncovering a wordmark instead of a fade
a smear that grips the athletes and refuses to touch the sky

everything arriving in the wake of something that just crossed the frame

templates.title: Voxelia
templates.description: A one-screen, cobalt-blue, pixel-art-flavoured hero for a fictional real-time chess studio. The whole page floats on a field of slowly drifting pixel waves — chunky blocks of two close blues, quantised to five shades, rippling lazily under the cursor. Over it, a hairline-ruled layout shell: logo, centred nav and a white contact pill in the top bar, then three columns — a Jersey-25 pixel headline with copy and CTA on the left, a live 3D chess scene in a near-black navy card at the centre, and a 2×2 grid of oversized stat figures on the right. Inside the card a glowing white king bobs, spins and leans toward the pointer while twelve glossy black-chrome pieces orbit it under a real rigid-body simulation: a per-piece magnet breathes them in and out, capsule contacts make them collide and tumble, and a cursor swipe shoves them coasting for seconds before the shell spring reels them back. Boot is a pixel flood — a white curtain flooded from the centre by the hero's blues in dithered 16px cells while a corner counter climbs, holding at 92 until the scene is genuinely running — then the page assembles itself block by block as the swarm snaps onto the king. On desktop the native cursor is replaced by a tiny spinning 3D pointer in its own 104px WebGL canvas that swaps to a fixed three-quarter 'hover' variant over anything interactive.

templates.title: Wanderlust
templates.description: A landing page for a small-group adventure travel company, built as one continuous exposure rather than a stack of blocks. It opens on a counting preloader, hands over to aerial footage of a glacial river valley played at 2x, and then assembles its interface AROUND a brightened window cut into that footage — the window arrives first and alone, scaling up from 0.62 like a lens opening on the shot, and the wordmark, display type, captions and destination list gather after it on a 55ms stagger. The clip's own last frame is dissolved over it in full resolution the moment the footage stops, because that frame is the one the encoder spent the fewest bits on and is also the one the reader is left looking at. Below it: sixteen polaroid postcards scattered across a near-black gallery, every one on the scene at once, flying in from off-frame along directions stepped by the golden angle and tilting toward the cursor when you point at their country; a pinned photographic manifesto whose three-line headline writes itself word by word while the backdrop pans half its height; four full-bleed panels that widen as you point at them and restack into a vertical scroll below 1024; and a layered mountain CTA where a pinned note writes itself onto the view and the footer rides up over the scene as frosted glass. The whole page is written in one warm cream at four alphas, on true black under the media and a near-black everywhere else, with a single saturated red reserved for a camera's tally lamp.
